title: Temporal Access Provenance & SIEM Ingest Shim Spec
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a compact, time-aware provenance model and a lightweight SIEM ingest shim to support RBAC v2 evidence automation. Goal is to enable compact audit exports that preserve temporal ordering, proof-of-origin, and fast downstream correlation for SIEMs without exploding event volume.

Background / problem summary:
- RBAC v2 introduces ephemeral tokens, timebound grants, and transient delegations; downstream SIEMs currently receive flat auth events that lose the temporal relationships (start/end, delegation chains).
- Security and Product want both: (a) compact, queryable evidence bundles for forensic queries, and (b) retained ability to feed per-event streams into SIEM for alerts.
- Current naive approach: emit every grant/change + every access event -> high cardinality + cost.

High-level goals:
- Represent access evidence as: provenance header + minimal per-request fingerprint.
- Make bundles compact (epoched snapshots + delta events) and verifiable (signable metadata).
- Provide a shim layer that converts provenance bundles into SIEM-friendly events and keeps linkage IDs for rehydration.
- Support canary rollout and partial sampling to manage SIEM SLOs.

Design overview:
1) Provenance Epochs: group evidence into epochs (e.g., 5m default). Each epoch contains: list of active grants/roles, delegation edges with timestamps, and a small manifest. Epochs are immutable once closed and get an epoch-id = UTC-iso + monotonic counter.

2) Compact per-request token (Access Fingerprint): every request that needs audit emits a tiny fingerprint: {epoch_id, resource_hash, actor_id_hash, op_code, seq_hint}. Fingerprint is <200 bytes. The heavy data (full grant objects, human principals) live in the epoch bundle stored in evidence-store (S3-like).

3) Epoch manifest and signing: when an epoch closes, the system computes a manifest (SHA256 of sorted grant descriptors) and signs it with the internal evidence key (KMS-backed). Signature stored in manifest metadata and optionally pushed to SIEM as proof-of-origin event.

4) SIEM ingest shim responsibilities:
- Accept stream of fingerprints + manifest-signature events.
- Expand fingerprint into richer event only on alerting / analyst request by resolving epoch_id -> grab manifest from evidence-store using signed manifest.
- Emit two classes to SIEM: "audit-lite" (every request fingerprint) and "audit-rich" (manifest linkage events + occasional full-grant snapshots per epoch).
- Provide backpressure controls and sampling knobs per workspace/customer so SIEM ingestion rate can be tuned.

5) Evidence TTL and archival:
- Live evidence-store retention default: 90 days, then archive to cold store for 2 years.
- Signed manifest provides integrity for archived bundles. For legal holds we mark epochs as pinned.

Event model (fields we propose):
- epoch_id: string (e.g., 20240821T1345Z-0003)
- actor_fingerprint: hex(sha1(actor_id + salt))
- resource_hash: hex(sha1(resource_id))
- op_code: short enum (AUTHZ_CHECK, TOKEN_ISSUE, DELEGATE_CREATE, DELEGATE_REVOKE)
- seq_hint: uint32 (optional monotonic per-connection non-unique)
- clock_skew_hint: ms (optional)
- manifest_sig: base64(sig) (only for manifest events)
- evidence_url: presigned url or storage locator (for manual resolution)

Privacy considerations:
- No PII in fingerprints. actor_fingerprint is salted per-org; salt rotation policy documented.
- Evidence-store access is ACLed; SIEM receives only hashes and epoch linkage unless workspace opts-in to full snapshots.

Verification & replay:
- Forensics tool: given seq of fingerprints + epoch_id, the tool fetches manifest, verifies signature, reconstructs role graph and replay authorizations for a timeframe.

Shim implementation notes (engineering):
- Lightweight Go service co-located with ingress; exposes a write API: /audit/fingerprint (HTTP/GRPC).
- Internally writes fingerprints to Kafka topic "audit.fingerprints" and manifests to "audit.manifests". SIEM connector tail-reads topics and writes to SIEM and to evidence-store.
- Danger: fanout from Kafka -> SIEM can be huge; add an adaptive sampler in connector.

Rollout plan (staged):
Phase 0 - experiments (1 sprint):
- Build shim prototype, emit audit-lite for internal traffic only.
- Run replay tool against subset of production logs to confirm reconstructability.

Phase 1 - limited opt-in (4 weeks):
- Enable epoching for 20% of orgs (low-traffic orgs). SIEM receives audit-lite + epoch manifests at low frequency.
- Monitor: SIEM event growth, average manifest fetch latency, evidence-store egress rates.

Phase 2 - sampling + canary (8 weeks):
- Expose sampling knobs per-tenant (1%, 10%, 100% for different event classes).
- Enable "rich-on-alert" mode: SIEM connector will expand to audit-rich only when SIEM raises an alert.

Phase 3 - full opt-out / defaults (quarter):
- Make epoching default for all RBAC v2 traffic with conservative sampling (e.g., 5% audit-rich).
- Documentation + runbooks + SOC onboarding.

Migration checklist (from current flat-event model):
- Add fingerprint fields to existing authorizer emission path (backwards compatible).
- Deploy shim in parallel with current exporter; compare counts for 2 weeks.
- Switch SIEM parsing rules to prefer epoch linkage fields; keep fallback to old flat events during transition.
- Mark epoch manifests pinned for first 30 days after migration for easier debugging.

Operational runbook (short):
- If SIEM shows gaps: check Kafka lag on "audit.fingerprints" and connector error rate.
- If manifest fetches failing: verify evidence-store presign rotation and KMS key access.
- Incident quick-fix: flip tenant to full snapshot mode and rerun export for timeframe.

Open questions (needs team decisions):
- epoch duration: 5m default vs 1m/10m tradeoffs (latency vs manifest size).
- signature algorithm and long-term key rotation cadence.
- sampling default per tier (free vs paid vs enterprise).
- exact schema SIEM favors for parsing (RFC vs custom fields).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- [Asha] write prototype spec for Go shim APIs and submit PR (GH-PR-1289) - due 2024-09-08.
- [Luis] spike Kafka connector sampler implementation and perf test - due 2024-09-20.
- [Priya] coordinate with SOC on SIEM field mapping and retention policy - due 2024-09-15.
- [Tom] draft Confluence runbook and legal hold integration notes - due 2024-09-22.

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- offline: Kayla suggested adding per-resource compaction window for hot endpoints (e.g., authn endpoints where we expect high qps). worth profiling.
- Slack thread: #sec-authz contains early designs, see thread ts=1713432000 for whiteboard doodles.

Appendix: quick example flow
- t=00:00:00 epoch open 20240821T0000Z-0001 -> contains grants G1, G2 signed -> manifest_sig M1.
- client request -> emit fingerprint {epoch: 20240821T0000Z-0001, actor_fingerprint: ab12..., resource_hash: 9f3..., op: AUTHZ_CHECK}
- SIEM receives fingerprint events for alerting; on alert, SOC clicks linkage id and the UI requests evidence-store->manifest M1 -> full grant graph reconstructed.

This is a working draft. I expect follow-ups to tighten the schema, decide signing/rotation policy, and finalize sampling defaults.
